replacements.before: Example (Module 11). If $V\ge0$ and $V(x_{t+1})\le V(x_t)$, then $V(x_t)\to v^\ast\ge0$, but nothing forces $v^\ast=0$ ($1+\frac1{t+1}$ decreases to $1$); that needs compactness and strict decrease (end of Section 6). For $x_{t+1}=x_t/(1+x_t^2)$, $V(x)=x^2$, $x_0=1$, the values $1,\ 0.25,\ 0.16,\ 0.119,\ 0.095,\dots$ decrease and converge. Pointwise vs uniform: $f_n\to f$ pointwise if $f_n(x)\to f(x)$ for each $x$ ($T$ may depend on $x$), uniformly if $\sup_x|f_n(x)-f(x)|\to0$; $x^n\to0$ pointwise on $[0,1)$ but not uniformly. On a finite set pointwise implies uniform (take the largest $T$).
